# Review 2026-11-28: first judgement pass (10 biggest surprises, Oct 27 - Nov 27)

| Idea | Our call | Move | Verdict | What really moved it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BRBR | watch long (whey relief) | +77% | lucky | New CEO's self-help margin plan; protein costs guided UP |
| CVI | watch short (cracks) | -47% | lucky | Half cracks; half a levered, dilutive $4.2B refinery deal (Icahn) |
| DINO | watch short (cracks) | -24% | right reason | Diesel cracks normalised; beat ignored |
| TBLD.L | long (traded) | -27% | reasoning error | Confirmed good news = sell-the-news after a 30% run on public Steam data |
| ABY.AX | watch long (DJ share) | -41% | signal missed | Warehouse/ERP cutover chaos, guidance cut 3 days before the AGM |
| CRCL | watch long (Jan rule) | -23% | unrelated | Crypto beta; catalyst not yet tested |
| CAPR | pass (FDA coin flip) | -69% | signal missed | Second CRL; record (9-3 AdCom, prior CRL) skewed it |
| TTWO | avoid | +19% | signal missed | GTA VI pre-orders/reviews/launch, all dated and visible |
| IREN | avoid (wait) | -48% | right reason | AI data-centre financing fear, unfunded capex |
| AMD | avoid (priced) | -27% | lucky | One-third reversal; two-thirds a short-seller report on China exports |

## Patterns (hypotheses, n=10)
1. **We under-use dated catalysts with visible evidence** (TTWO, CAPR, BRBR, ABY): the information was public and dated; we
   stayed neutral or waited for the wrong date. Fix: binary-event and dated-catalyst rules added to Opus's research checks;
   watch re-checks (brain.recheck_watch) already in place.
2. **Public-data drivers get priced before the announcement** (TBLD): confirmation becomes sell-the-news. Fix: "noticed"
   check now compares the move since the data first showed and broker targets.
3. **Our right directions were often right for other reasons** (BRBR, CVI, AMD): the real drivers were company actions
   (self-help plans, deals, short reports). These go to the movers bank so the swarm hunts their early signs.
4. **Avoid/wait calls were our best** (IREN, AMD, DINO watch): judgement on what not to buy is sound; conversion of good
   short ideas into trades is the gap (DINO/CVI never traded).

All ten are filed in knowledge/movers/ with early signs and "look for next time" rules.
reflections/2026-11-27-lead-review.md:
# Preliminary judgement of the desk's ideas, 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-27 (from ledger/REPORT.md)

Benchmark: SPY fell ~7% from Oct 27 (S&P closed more than 10% below its October high in late November).

## Headline
- Ideas we did NOT act on: 18/25 right vs benchmark, average edge +9.6%.
- Ideas we DID act on: 1/5 right, average edge -12.9%. Paper equity -4.2% on five trades.
- Our judgement about what to avoid was good; our choice of what to actually buy was bad.

## What worked (and we mostly didn't trade)
- Refiners short thesis (cracks falling, stocks pricing peak margins): all seven fell 12-47% (CVI -47%). Left on "watch".
- BRBR (whey costs easing): +73% after the Nov 17 report. Left on "watch".
- Oil after the midterms: right (-11% since); planned entry came after the move.
- Avoid calls: AI/miner rebound (IREN -51%, CIFR -32%), AMD after its +21% week (-31%), Myer at 0.25 (-10%).
- Earnings numbers: 6/6 times we leaned the right side of consensus; 5/8 ranges hit.

## What failed
- Every long we took in a falling market: OSUR (-17%), tinyBuild (stopped -13.5% despite a record-breaking game), W, RIG.
- Watch-longs: ABY (-41%), uranium (-23%), CRCL (-24%). Calibration: "S&P -10% by Feb" at 30% happened within two weeks.

## Lessons for the autonomous desk
1. Trade the bearish theses too: in this tape our short ideas were the best ones.
2. A watch with a dated trigger (BRBR's Nov 17 report) should become an armed order, not a note.
3. Measured drivers still lose to market beta: size down or hedge longs when the index is breaking down.
4. Probabilities for macro tail events were too low; treat regime breaks as more likely while correlation resets.

# Movers: regulatory or legal
Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## CAPR from 2026-10-27: -68%
- What actually moved it: Nov 20: second Complete Response Letter for deramiocel (no substantial evidence of effectiveness) plus FDA allegations of data integrity violations; $7.59 -> $1.92 (-75%).
- Early signs (observable beforehand): July 2026 AdCom 9-3 against; July 2025 CRL citing the same deficiency; PDUFA extension only after narrowing the indication; +76% run-up into the decision (cause unverified).
- Look for next time: PDUFA after a negative AdCom plus a prior CRL: assume the FDA leans to rejection and treat the event as skewed, not a coin flip; a run-up into it adds downside.
- Our call: pass (manual): FDA decision Nov 22 priced as a lottery, no probability edge. Verdict signal_missed, signal played_out, moved by driver.
- Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001133869/000110465926130730/capr-ex99d1.htm https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/capricor-fda-duchenne-cell-therapy-deramiocel/875384/

## CRCL from 2026-11-12: -24% (-1.2 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Crypto selloff (BTC 71.3k -> 59.8k, Nov 12-28) plus the Nov 4 Q3 overhang: reserve income -8% on a ~3.5% reserve yield, USDC flat y/y at $73.9B, revenue flattered by a one-off $182m token presale; World Bank/Citi USDC news on Nov 17 did not help.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): BTC already rolling over on the flag day; Q3 showed flat USDC and falling reserve income; CRCL in a steady downtrend from $81.
- Look for next time: Crypto-adjacent longs with a distant regulatory catalyst: gate entry on BTC/COIN trend and USDC supply growth; a far-off rule date does not offset crypto beta.
- Our call: watch_long (manual): Stablecoin rule effective Jan 18 vs beaten-down issuer. Verdict unrelated, signal unclear, moved by market.
- Sources: https://www.tikr.com/blog/circle-sinks-10-as-crypto-stocks-slide-and-mizuho-calls-q3-uneventful https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-3-2261353-20261118

# Movers: commodity price
Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## DINO from 2026-10-27: -25% (+1.5 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Refining margin normalisation: Russian diesel output recovering after export quotas (Reuters ~Oct 27), diesel crack $102 mid-Oct -> $83 by Nov 5, Brent -18.5% in two weeks to ~Nov 15, US diesel below $6; Oct 28 Q3 beat (adj. EPS $11.75 vs ~$7.8) ignored on peak-earnings worries; sector selloff Nov 18 with no news.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): Diesel/jet cracks already off mid-October peaks ($102 -> $92 by Oct 23); refiner equities peaked ~Oct 13; peers selling off on beats (Valero Oct 22); supply response visible (Russian export quotas).
- Look for next time: Refiners selling off on record beats while cracks are off their peak and a supply response is visible (export quotas, restarts) = confirmation for a short; track the weekly diesel crack and the CRAK ETF.
- Our call: watch_short (manual): Refiners price peak cracks as durable while diesel cracks fall. Verdict right_reason, signal played_out, moved by driver.

# Movers: guidance change
Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## BRBR from 2026-10-29: +73% (+5.5 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 18 FY26 Q4: sales +7% to $692.0M (beat); FY27 adj. EBITDA guided $310-350M vs $288.8M despite flat-to-down sales, via low double-digit shake price increases, >=$100M 3-yr supply-chain savings, ~400bp gross margin expansion and lapping ~$37M inventory charges; new CEO trades growth for margin. +24% on the day ($11.01 -> $13.66), $16.08 by Nov 27. Nov 16 7-Eleven distribution deal helped into the print.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): 52-week low $7.33 on Oct 1 (crushed multiple); already +20% from our flag into the print; 7-Eleven deal Nov 16; dated print with a new CEO. Whey relief was never the swing factor: Aug Q3 call already pointed to continued inflation and price actions.
- Look for next time: Crushed multiple + dated print + new CEO: watch for EBITDA guided back to growth via self-help (pricing + savings) rather than waiting for input costs; check hedge cover before assuming spot commodity relief reaches the P&L.
- Our call: watch_long (manual): Whey protein costs easing from June record; needs FY27 cost commentary (Nov 17). Verdict lucky, signal failed, moved by other_news.
- Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772016/000162828026074645/brbrexh991-q42026earningsr.htm https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/bellring-brbr-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/18/why-bellring-brands-stock-surged-today/

## ABY.AX from 2026-11-05: -42% (-1.7 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 16 FY27 trading update: product revenue -8.0% over 20 weeks; new National Distribution Centre ramp caused out-of-stocks; FY27 EBITDA guidance cut to $4.0-6.5m from $9-13m, revenue guidance withdrawn. A$0.265 -> A$0.15.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): FY26 Appendix 4E (Aug 24): EBITDA -39% to $3.8m, weak Q4, DC and ERP cutover in July 2026, FY27 guidance needing 2.4-3.4x EBITDA; thin volume meant any miss would gap.
- Look for next time: Micro-caps mid-way through a DC/ERP cutover tend to warn before the AGM; discount 'share gain from a competitor's collapse' until the company reports revenue growth.
- Our call: watch_long (manual): Prestige beauty share from DJ; tiny cap (needs closure list/AGM). Verdict signal_missed, signal failed, moved by other_news.
- Sources: https://kalkine.com.au/news/announcements/adore-beauty-group-cuts-fy27-underlying-ebitda-guidance-to-4065m-at-2026-agm https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260824/pdf/07332lpnhbk2rp.pdf

# Movers: short squeeze or positioning
Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## TBLD.L from 2026-10-30: -27% (-1.6 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 12 07:00 Trading Update: FY26 revenue $54-56m, adj. EBITDA $7-8m 'ahead of market expectations', Probably Stolen >1M copies, ReStory and Graveyard Keeper 2 >500k each. Sell-the-news: 13.0p -> 11.5p on the heaviest volume of the period, then 9.25p by Nov 25. No placing or director dealing; Probably Stolen live players ~21k on Nov 28 (-88% from peak).
- Early signs (observable beforehand): Run 10.6p -> 13.75p (Oct 27 -> Nov 3) on 10x volume = the public CCU news was already bought; broker targets ~9p below price; a dated confirming RNS was likely after record CCUs; CCU decay after the Nov 4 peak was visible on Steam.
- Look for next time: When the driver is public data (Steam CCU, app ranks) and the stock has already re-rated, treat the confirming announcement as sell-the-news; compare broker targets with the price before entry.
- Our call: long (manual): Probably Stolen Steam record. Verdict reasoning_error, signal played_out, moved by other_news.
- Sources: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/tinybuild-inc-di-reg-s-cat-3---tbld/trading-update/9871218 https://www.londonstockexchange.com/en/news/article/TBLD/trading-update/a290-e2-6f-01-d4-4469a2 https://api.steampowered.com/ISteamUserStats/GetNumberOfCurrentPlayers/v1/?appid=4348910

## CVI from 2026-10-27: -47% (+2.7 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 3: record Q3 (adj. EPS $4.00 vs ~$2.5-2.9) plus a $4.2B purchase of Marathon's St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries funded by a $2.5B secured bridge, $500M from Icahn Enterprises, $800M from Trafigura and a $750M share offering ($250M secondary by an IEP unit); dividend held at $0.10. -13% that day, $38 by Nov 6; then the refiner selloff (diesel crack $102 -> $83, Brent -18.5%) took it to ~$30.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): Cracks rolling over from mid-October and Russian diesel export quotas (Reuters ~Oct 27) were visible; the deal itself was not signalled, but Icahn's history of using CVI for deals plus a windfall cash pile were standing risks.
- Look for next time: Controlled refiners (Icahn/IEP) sitting on a windfall quarter: price in a levered, dilutive deal or the controlling holder selling into strength on the print date, on top of cracks normalising.
- Our call: watch_short (manual): Refiners price peak cracks as durable while diesel cracks fall. Verdict lucky, signal played_out, moved by other_news.
- Sources: https://finviz.com/news/414996/cvr-energy-posts-a-record-refining-quarter-and-bets-the-windfall-on-a-levered-marathon-deal https://www.ibtimes.com.au/cvr-energy-shares-fall-marathon-refinery-deal-1877874 https://investinglive.com/commodities/oil-cracks-are-beginning-to-fall-and-refineries-are-pointing-to-more-normalization/

# Movers: financing or dilution
Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## IREN from 2026-10-29: -51% (+2.0 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 4 report that Childress site delays made Microsoft defer capex (-11.4%); Nov 5 post-midterm chip wipeout (-17%) and Q1 FY27 results showing ~$15B remaining FY27 capex with ~$6B unfunded and the >$4B ARR target slipping to early 2027; from Nov 9 bank reluctance to finance data centres (Reuters) and peer target slips (Nebius) drove the slide.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): Microsoft's late-October capex shortfall from delayed third-party capacity; Applied Digital saying ~800MW still needed financing; neocloud group -13% Oct 26 - Nov 2; The Information's Childress delay story the day before results.
- Look for next time: Capex-heavy neoclouds/miners: hyperscaler 'delayed third-party capacity' comments, peers' unfunded-capex disclosures and bank-lending headlines turning sour = move from wait to avoid (or short).
- Our call: avoid (manual): AI/miner rebound: wait for earnings/CPI/NVDA. Verdict right_reason, signal played_out, moved by other_news.
- Sources: https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/iren-stock-drops-after-report-says-it-s-behind-microsoft-s-ai-spending-delay-as-investors-turn-to-earnings/cNG15gfR9Ef https://www.analyticsinsight.net/news/iren-stock-falls-17-as-bitcoin-mining-revenue-drops-58-and-ai-expansion-accelerates https://www.tikr.com/blog/iren-sinks-13-in-a-week-as-big-techs-results-rattle-neoclouds-already-popping

Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## AMD from 2026-11-12: -31% (+1.7 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 13 reversal of the post-Huang-resignation rally as the 10-year hit ~5.17% on hot PPI and OpenAI (AMD's big customer) reported a $10.9B quarterly operating loss; Nov 16 sector selloff on export-control talk; Nov 19 Hunterbrook short report alleging blacklisted IEIT kept receiving AMD firmware (22.4% of 2025 revenue billed to China/HK), days after tighter US chip rules for Southeast Asia; AMD disputes it.
- Early signs (observable beforehand): One-event +21% week into rising yields; for the short report none, though Southeast Asia export tightening and Dec 1 House hearings on chip exports were visible days earlier.
- Look for next time: Fade a one-event 20%+ surge in a mega-cap chip stock into rising yields; flag China/HK revenue share plus fresh export-rule headlines as short-report tail risk.
- Our call: avoid (manual): Rotation winner already priced after +21% week. Verdict lucky, signal played_out, moved by other_news.
- Sources: https://www.tikr.com/blog/amd-sinks-9-marvell-down-5-as-chip-rally-reverses-and-treasury-yields-hit-5 https://www.ibtimes.com/amd-shares-fall-hunterbrook-china-export-risks-3809979 https://fool.com/investing/2026/11/19/why-amd-stock-was-plunging-on-thursday

# Movers: product launch
Real causes of big moves the desk judged, and what preceded them.

## TTWO from 2026-10-29: +18% (-2.7 sigma vs its normal moves)
- What actually moved it: Nov 9 Q2 FY27: revenue miss but FY revenue forecast raised and CEO said GTA VI pre-orders 'far in excess of our initial expectations' (+8.3% Nov 10); near-perfect reviews Nov 18 (+6.2%); launch Nov 19 with third-party estimates of ~17M copies / $1.65-1.84B day-one (unofficial).
- Early signs (observable beforehand): Launch date confirmed May 22; pre-launch Sensor Tower estimate ~9.7M units / $942M, already above GTA V's record; 31M-viewer Netflix preview; stock -19% YTD into the print.
- Look for next time: A dated mega-launch with record third-party pre-order data: a stock drifting lower into it is a setup, not a reason to avoid.
- Our call: avoid (manual): Falling into GTA VI launch, no run-up to ride. Verdict signal_missed, signal failed, moved by driver.
